sentences.text: Changchengopterus is a non-pterodactyloid pterosaur found in Qinglong County, Hebei Province, China.
Scientists have described a second adult specimen with lower jaws from the Paleontological Museum of Liaoning.
The type species Changchengopterus pani was described by Lü Junchang in 2009 from fossils found in the Callovian-aged Tiaojishan Formation.
The species name pani honors Pan Lijun, who collected and donated the fossil to science.
In its original description, Changchengopterus was placed in the family Rhamphorhynchidae as a primitive pterosaur related to Dorygnathus.
A 2010 study tentatively placed Changchengopterus in the family Wukongopteridae due to noted similarities.
A 2013 study found Changchengopterus outside Wukongopteridae but slightly closer to pterodactyloids within the group Monofenestrata.
A 2017 analysis recovered Changchengopterus outside the group Monofenestrata.
A 2024 study included Changchengopterus within Pterodactyliformes, suggesting primitive monofenestratans are an evolutionary grade leading to Pterodactyloidea.
Changchengopterus is classified within the unranked group Monofenestrata.
Changchengopterus is classified within the family Wukongopteridae.
Fossils of Changchengopterus come from the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic.
Changchengopterus lived between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian to Kimmeridgian stages.
